title: Business Loans & Working Capital
headline: Give your next move the funding it needs.
intro: A new contract, extra capacity or a recurring cash-flow gap. Explore borrowing around what the business needs to achieve and how it expects to repay.
summary: Term loans, revolving credit and overdrafts for business investment and working capital.
uses: Business term loans
Borrow an agreed amount and repay over a defined period. A term loan can support expansion or expenditure that is not tied to one financed asset.
Revolving credit
Draw, repay and draw again within an agreed limit and availability period. Useful where the amount needed changes through the trading cycle.
Business overdrafts
An agreed facility linked to a bank account can cover short-term cash movements. It is different from a term loan and is generally repayable on demand.
steps: Define the requirement
Separate a one-off investment from a cash gap that repeats. Set out the amount, timing and purpose.
Test repayment
Use current trading and forecasts to assess headroom alongside existing borrowing.
Compare the facility
Review total cost, security, drawdown rules and repayment or renewal conditions.
terms: Security and guarantees
Secured lending takes security over agreed assets. Unsecured lending may still require a personal guarantee.
Cost of flexibility
Revolving facilities can carry arrangement, renewal and unused-limit charges as well as interest. Compare the whole commitment.
Renewal and demand
An overdraft or renewable facility is not permanent capital. Understand review dates, cancellation rights and repayment triggers.
prepare: Amount, purpose and required date
Recent accounts, cash-flow forecasts and existing borrowing
Expected repayment source and security position
faqs: Is a loan or revolving facility better?
A term loan suits a defined borrowing need; a revolving facility may fit changing cash requirements. Compare cost and repayment against the actual cash cycle.
Can a new business apply?
The trading history, evidence, security and provider criteria matter. We can discuss the requirement without assuming that a particular route is available.
Can we refinance existing borrowing?
Potentially. Settlement charges, remaining terms and the cost of the replacement facility all need to be considered.
valueHeading: Build the borrowing around the cash flow.
valueIntro: We help separate a temporary timing gap from a longer-term investment, then organise the figures behind the repayment case. That makes it easier to compare the actual facility rather than a headline rate.

title: Asset & Equipment Finance
headline: Put the right equipment to work.
intro: Buy, lease or refinance the assets behind your business. From a single machine to a fleet investment, start with what you need the equipment to do.
summary: Finance for buying equipment, using it through a lease or releasing value from assets you own.
uses: Buy and work towards ownership
Hire purchase spreads the purchase cost while keeping the asset in use. Ownership follows the agreement’s payment and purchase conditions.
Lease for productive use
Compare finance leases and residual value structures around how long you need the equipment and what happens at the end.
Release existing asset value
Refinance can turn available equity in machinery into business cash, subject to valuation, ownership and existing finance.
steps: Describe the asset
Confirm the specification, supplier, price and whether it is new or used.
Choose the outcome
Decide whether you want eventual ownership, a period of use or cash released from an existing asset.
Match the commitment
Compare deposit, term, repayments, maintenance and end-of-term obligations with the operating plan.
terms: Eligible equipment
Asset type, age, condition, supplier and resale market affect the assessment. Software and installation may need separate treatment.
Rental fleets
Permission to hire equipment onward must be confirmed. Financing an operator’s fleet is different from funding a dealer’s sale stock.
Ownership and risk
Understand who owns the asset, who insures and maintains it, and what happens if payments are missed.
prepare: Equipment description, supplier and quote
New or used status, intended use and delivery date
Deposit, existing finance and preferred ownership outcome
faqs: Can used machinery be financed?
It may be considered, depending on the asset, supplier, age, condition and provider. A used asset is not automatically excluded or accepted.
Does this include technology?
Equipment and some technology investments can be considered. Licences, integration and services need a separate cost breakdown.
Can we fund a hire fleet?
That is a requirement we can discuss. Tell us how assets will be hired out so onward-hire permission and the appropriate structure can be assessed.
valueHeading: Connect the asset to the operating plan.
valueIntro: We bring the purchase, intended use and cash commitment together before exploring provider conversations. A machine, a rental fleet and a software project need different questions, even when they support the same growth plan.

title: Hire Purchase
headline: Own the equipment. Spread the investment.
intro: Equip the business now and spread the purchase cost over an agreed period, with a clear route to ownership at the end.
summary: Purchase finance for machinery, equipment and vehicles where ownership is the objective.
uses: Add capacity
Fund equipment for a new contract or an increase in demand without paying the whole purchase price at the outset.
Replace a working asset
Plan a replacement around the machine’s useful life, reliability and contribution to the business.
Build a fleet
Assess individual purchases or a wider fleet programme, with rental use disclosed from the start.
steps: Agree the purchase
Identify the supplier, asset, price and initial contribution. The provider assesses both the business and equipment.
Use and repay
Use the asset while making agreed payments. Insurance, maintenance and operating costs remain part of the budget.
Complete ownership
For HP, ownership usually requires all sums due and any purchase option payment. Under conditional sale, title passes when the contractual conditions are met.
terms: Deposit and VAT
Confirm the initial contribution, VAT timing and other upfront costs rather than assuming they are all financed.
Final payments
A balloon can reduce regular instalments but leaves a larger final payment. Plan how that will be met.
Early exit
Settlement terms and charges vary. The asset cannot be treated as freely owned while the agreement remains outstanding.
prepare: Supplier quote and asset specification
Deposit available and intended purchase date
Trading information, existing commitments and any onward-hire use
faqs: How is conditional sale different?

Both can spread purchase costs. HP normally includes an option to purchase; conditional sale commits the buyer to purchase, with title passing under its conditions. The agreement determines the rights and obligations.
Can we sell the equipment during the term?
You will generally need to settle the finance or obtain the provider’s agreement before disposal.
Is leasing an alternative?
Yes. Leasing may suit a business focused on use rather than ownership. Compare the full term and end-of-term options.
valueHeading: Make ownership part of a workable plan.
valueIntro: We help set out the purchase, deposit and repayment requirement, including any final payment. The aim is a clear provider conversation about the equipment and the business that will use it.

title: Equipment Leasing
headline: Get the capability. Plan the commitment.
intro: Use the equipment your business needs through regular rentals. Choose the structure around the working life of the asset and your plans for replacement.
summary: Finance lease and operating or residual value structures for eligible business equipment.
uses: Finance lease
The provider owns the equipment while the business uses it. The business typically carries much of the operating risk and responsibility.
Operating and residual value structures
Some structures price rentals around expected value at the end. Asset eligibility, usage and return conditions are important.
Planned replacement
A lease can support an equipment replacement cycle, but renewal, return and replacement are contractual choices rather than automatic entitlements.
steps: Set the use period
Define the equipment, expected hours or usage and how long the business needs it.
Compare structures
Look at initial rental, regular payments, responsibilities and the treatment of residual value.
Plan the end
Check notice periods and whether the options include return, continued hire or a third-party sale arrangement.
terms: Legal ownership
A lease does not automatically transfer ownership to the business. Do not assume the final rental buys the equipment.
Return conditions
Wear, usage, condition, transport and disposal obligations can affect the total cost.
Tax and accounting
Treatment depends on the agreement and circumstances. Review it with your accountant; a lease is not automatically off balance sheet.
prepare: Equipment quote and expected usage
Preferred term and replacement plans
Maintenance arrangements and any rental-fleet use
faqs: Are all leases the same?
No. Finance leases and operating or residual value structures allocate risks and end-of-term obligations differently. Product names alone do not establish the terms.
Will maintenance be included?
Only if the agreement or a separate service package includes it. Confirm insurance, repairs and maintenance explicitly.
Can we keep using the equipment at the end?
Some agreements permit continued hire. Check availability, notice requirements and further rental costs before committing.
valueHeading: Compare the use, the cost and the way out.
valueIntro: We help explain how long you need the equipment and which responsibilities the business can support. That provides a useful basis for comparing lease structures and their end-of-term conditions.

title: Asset Refinance
headline: Release value from the assets you already have.
intro: Machinery can support the business beyond the work it does. Explore whether available equity in existing equipment could provide cash for your next requirement.
summary: Release eligible asset equity through structures such as sale and HP back or sale and leaseback.
uses: Release working capital
Explore cash tied up in owned machinery while keeping eligible equipment in operational use.
Support an investment
Assess whether asset equity could contribute to an expansion or another defined business purpose.
Review existing finance
Consider replacement funding alongside settlement costs, remaining obligations and the amount actually released.
steps: Establish ownership
Identify the assets, legal owner, purchase history and any existing lender interest.
Assess available equity
A provider valuation and any debt settlement determine potential net proceeds, not the original invoice price alone.
Agree the structure
Sale and HP back provides a route back to ownership. Sale and leaseback gives continued use under lease terms.
terms: Existing debt
Outstanding finance must be addressed. Compare net cash released after settlement and transaction costs.
Asset suitability
Age, condition, evidence of title and the resale market can affect eligibility and valuation.
A new obligation
Releasing cash introduces payments and potential loss of the asset on default. Test repayment alongside operational needs.
prepare: Asset register, purchase evidence and estimated values
Existing finance agreements and settlement figures
Cash required, purpose and repayment capacity
faqs: Must the asset be fully paid for?
Not always, but existing finance and security need to be settled or accommodated with the relevant providers’ agreement.
Can we refinance an older machine?
Provider rules differ. The asset’s age, condition, useful life and value will be assessed.
Is this the same as a general business loan?
No. The transaction is linked to identified assets and may transfer legal ownership during the agreement.
valueHeading: See the cash release and the new commitment.
valueIntro: We help organise the asset information, existing finance and purpose of the funds. The useful comparison is the net cash available and the future obligation, not the headline valuation alone.

title: Vehicle & Fleet Finance
headline: Keep your business moving.
intro: From a delivery van to a commercial fleet, compare buying and hiring around the vehicles’ role, usage and replacement cycle.
summary: Purchase and lease options for business vehicles and operational fleets.
uses: Hire purchase
Work towards ownership through an agreed payment schedule, with any final payment included in the plan.
Vehicle leasing
Use vehicles through regular rentals, with ownership and end-of-term arrangements determined by the lease.
Contract hire
Hire a vehicle for a defined term and usage profile. Mileage, condition and any service package affect the commitment.
steps: Map the requirement
Set out vehicle types, number, new or used status and delivery dates.
Compare whole-life cost
Include initial payments, finance charges, servicing, insurance, usage limits and disposal or return costs.
Plan fleet changes
Allow for recruitment, demand changes, early termination and replacement timing.
terms: Use and condition
Mileage allowances and return standards matter for hire arrangements.
Commercial specifications
Payload, body conversions and specialist equipment need to be included in the quote and assessment.
Rental-company use
A business hiring vehicles to others needs a suitable facility and explicit permission; ordinary fleet funding does not establish that right.
prepare: Vehicle specifications, quotes and fleet size
Expected mileage, usage and replacement dates
Ownership preference and maintenance needs
faqs: Can used vehicles be considered?
Eligibility depends on the vehicle, age, condition, supplier and finance product.
Can electric vehicles be financed?
We can discuss the vehicle investment. Charging equipment and installation should be costed separately and assessed on their own terms.
Does contract hire include servicing?
Some packages include services, others do not. Compare the actual inclusions and exclusions.
valueHeading: Match the fleet decision to the business.
valueIntro: We help bring vehicle specifications, expected use and ownership preferences into one requirement. Compare the finance alongside running costs and replacement plans.
questionsHeading: Questions about your next vehicle or fleet.

title: Invoice Finance
headline: Keep trading while customers take time to pay.
intro: Turn eligible unpaid business invoices into working capital. Explore a facility that follows the sales ledger and the way your business collects payment.
summary: Factoring and invoice discounting against eligible business-to-business invoices.
uses: Invoice factoring
The provider typically supports collections and ledger administration as part of the arrangement.
Invoice discounting
The business generally retains credit control, with funding linked to eligible receivables. Confidential arrangements may be available.
A changing sales ledger
Availability can move with eligible invoices, customer payments and agreed limits rather than staying at one fixed amount.
steps: Review the ledger
Understand customers, credit terms, concentration, ageing and any disputed invoices.
Agree availability
The provider sets eligibility, advance rates, reserves and controls. Not every invoice will qualify.
Collect and recycle
Customer receipts reduce the balance and may create availability against further eligible invoices.
terms: Collections and visibility
Clarify who contacts customers, where they pay and whether the arrangement is disclosed.
Debtor risk
Retentions, set-off, disputes and concentrated customer exposure may reduce availability.
Charges and recourse
Compare service charges, discount charges, minimum fees and responsibility for unpaid debts. Bad-debt protection is not automatically included.
prepare: Aged debtor report and normal invoice terms
Customer concentration, disputes and contract terms
Turnover, funding need and existing security
faqs: Can equipment-hire invoices qualify?
Possibly. Hire terms, disputes, set-off rights and the quality of the debts need assessment.
Will our customers know?
That depends on the structure. Confidentiality is not a universal feature of invoice finance.
Does it protect us if a customer fails?
Not automatically. Any bad-debt protection must be separately specified, including exclusions and limits.
valueHeading: Start with the quality of the cash coming in.
valueIntro: We help explain the ledger, customer terms and funding gap before a provider approach. Factoring and discounting should be compared around the business’s collection process as well as the cash they could release.

title: Stock & Dealer Finance
headline: Keep stock available. Keep capital working.
intro: Finance equipment held for sale or demonstration, with a facility designed around the units you buy, hold and sell.
summary: Stocking and floorplan facilities for eligible dealers and equipment suppliers.
uses: Equipment held for sale
A stocking facility can fund eligible units while they wait for a buyer.
Demonstration equipment
Some arrangements can include demonstrators, subject to usage, asset and holding-period requirements.
Dealer and manufacturer networks
A facility may support a single dealer or a wider distribution arrangement, with individual units tracked.
steps: Define eligible stock
Confirm asset types, suppliers, unit values, expected holding periods and ownership.
Fund and track units
Finance is advanced under agreed limits and controls, often with reporting or stock checks.
Repay as units move
Sales, ageing limits or other contractual triggers determine when a unit must be repaid.
terms: Stock ageing
Curtailments or staged repayments can become due before a machine sells. Model a slower sales cycle.
Sale proceeds
Understand when the finance must be cleared and how title or security is released to the buyer.
Stock versus fleet
Long-term rental fleets are a different requirement. Any short-term hire use must be specifically permitted.
prepare: Stock list, unit values and supplier arrangements
Sales volumes, holding periods and demonstration or hire use
Existing stocking facilities and security
faqs: Is floorplan finance another name for stock finance?
Floorplan commonly describes unit-based dealer stocking finance. The actual assets, controls and repayment triggers depend on the facility.
Can lifting equipment be considered?
It is an asset category some providers consider. We need to establish the equipment, supplier, intended use and relevant provider appetite.
Can stock be imported?
Import transactions introduce supplier, shipment and payment requirements. A trade-finance route may also need to be considered.
valueHeading: Build funding around how stock moves.
valueIntro: We help distinguish sale stock, demonstrations and hire use, then set out the buying and selling cycle. A stocking conversation needs both unit-level detail and a credible plan for slower-moving inventory.

title: Trade & Import Finance
headline: Bridge the journey from supplier payment to customer cash.
intro: When suppliers need paying before a sale turns into cash, explore transaction-led funding around the goods, documents and trading cycle.
summary: Funding for eligible supplier payments and import transactions.
uses: Supplier-payment gaps
Support eligible purchases where the supplier is paid before the customer settles.
Imported goods
Assess funding alongside shipment evidence, delivery terms and the point at which the business takes control of the goods.
Trade documentation
Letters of credit and guarantees can address specific payment or performance risks. They are not interchangeable with a cash loan.
steps: Map the transaction
Identify the supplier, buyer, goods, countries, currency and payment dates.
Establish the evidence
A provider may require purchase orders, invoices, shipment documents and a track record of completing similar trades.
Match funding to receipts
Set the repayment plan around the transaction, with room for shipping, customs or customer-payment delays.
terms: Deposits and shipment
Advance deposits, pre-shipment costs and goods in transit may be treated differently. Do not assume the full purchase cycle is covered.
Supplier and country risk
Counterparty checks, permitted countries and documentation conditions affect the route.
Currency and timing
Exchange-rate changes and delays can alter the cash requirement. FX services are separate from the underlying funding.
prepare: Supplier and customer terms, orders and invoices
Countries, currency, shipment dates and transport documents
Gross margin, trading history and expected repayment
faqs: Can it fund machinery we import for resale?
That is a requirement to assess. Provider appetite depends on the goods, counterparties, documentation and repayment cycle.
What if we import equipment for our own fleet?
An asset-finance structure may be more appropriate. Deposits and pre-delivery payments need separate assessment.
Does a letter of credit provide working capital?
It is a conditional bank payment undertaking, not automatically a cash advance. Any associated funding is agreed separately.
valueHeading: Make the trading cycle clear from the start.
valueIntro: We help map the transaction, documents and timing before exploring a funding route. That makes the supplier-payment need and the proposed repayment easier to assess together.

title: Acquisition & Buyout Finance
headline: Fund the purchase. Support what comes next.
intro: Buy a business or take ownership through a management buyout, with funding that accounts for the purchase price and the business after completion.
summary: Debt and capital structures for acquisitions and management buyouts.
uses: Business acquisitions
Assess purchase funding alongside the target’s earnings, assets, integration costs and cash needs.
Management buyouts
Connect management’s investment, any external capital and the proposed debt with a credible ownership plan.
Acquisition programmes
A series of purchases needs a facility and operating plan that can support each transaction, not just the first.
steps: Build the transaction picture
Separate purchase consideration, fees, debt settlement and post-completion working capital.
Assess the funding mix
Compare cash-flow lending, asset-backed facilities, buyer equity and any seller funding.
Coordinate completion
Align diligence, legal conditions, existing lender releases and drawdown with the transaction timetable.
terms: Debt capacity
Historic earnings alone do not establish repayment capacity. Test the combined business and downside scenarios.
Ownership and control
Equity investment may change governance and shareholder rights. Debt creates repayment and covenant obligations.
Execution risk
Diligence findings, consents and legal documentation can change timing or terms. Funding is not committed simply because a purchase is agreed.
prepare: Target summary, price and proposed transaction structure
Buyer and target financials, forecasts and integration plan
Equity contribution, existing lenders and completion timetable
faqs: Can funding cover all of the purchase price?
The mix depends on the transaction and assessment. Do not assume a fully debt-funded purchase or no buyer contribution.
Can assets support the acquisition?
Eligible assets may support an ABL structure, subject to valuation, security and cash requirements after completion.
Can you help with preparation?
Financial modelling and transaction preparation can be commissioned separately for an agreed scope and fee.
valueHeading: Bring the transaction and funding work together.
valueIntro: We help organise the capital requirement and the provider questions around it. Financial models, investment materials or transaction workstreams can be commissioned separately where preparation is needed.

title: Asset Based Lending
headline: Bring the value across your assets together.
intro: A structured facility can combine eligible receivables, stock, machinery or property to support working capital, growth or a transaction.
summary: Combined funding against eligible business assets, rather than one isolated purchase.
uses: Working-capital headroom
Use a wider asset base to assess a facility around the business’s trading cycle.
Growth and acquisitions
Explore whether receivables, inventory and other assets could contribute to expansion or transaction funding.
Refinancing
Review a combined structure alongside existing lenders, settlement costs and security priorities.
steps: Map the asset base
Review eligible invoices, inventory, equipment and property, with evidence of ownership and current lending.
Structure availability
Valuations, advance rates, reserves and reporting define the borrowing base and any term components.
Manage the facility
Availability can change with asset values and eligibility. Reporting, audits and covenants form part of ongoing operation.
terms: Security and priority
Existing charges and lender consents can determine whether the proposed structure is workable.
Cash actually available
Gross asset values are not the same as net proceeds after reserves, existing debt and fees.
Reporting requirements
Factor in management time, valuation costs, audits and the effect of declining eligible assets on headroom.
prepare: Financial statements and forecasts
Debtor ageing, inventory and fixed-asset schedules
Existing facilities, charges and the funding purpose
faqs: How is this different from equipment finance?
Equipment finance usually relates to specific assets. ABL can combine several asset classes in one structured funding package.
Must we own property?
Not necessarily. The relevant asset mix depends on the business and provider; a facility may be based on other eligible assets.
Can ABL include a cash-flow loan?
Some structures combine asset-backed availability and term lending. That needs a separate repayment assessment.
valueHeading: Look across the assets and the existing obligations.
valueIntro: We help present the business’s asset base, current facilities and funding purpose as one coherent requirement. The structure needs to leave enough operating headroom after the transaction, not simply maximise the initial borrowing.
questionsHeading: Questions about a combined asset facility.

title: Finance for Your Customers
headline: Help customers buy the equipment you sell.
intro: Give buyers a route to explore finance alongside an equipment purchase, with clear responsibilities between your business, Frontier and the funding provider.
summary: A seller-facing finance arrangement using products such as hire purchase or leasing.
uses: Support equipment sales
Help business buyers consider spreading the cost instead of treating the full purchase price as the only route.
New and used stock
Establish which assets, suppliers and customer types a provider could consider.
A repeatable sales process
Agree how enquiries, quotations, information sharing and delivery milestones will be handled.
steps: Define the sales model
Share typical assets, buyers, transaction values and expected sales volumes.
Agree the arrangement
Confirm provider access, permitted introductions, customer consent and any commercial terms before presenting a programme.
Coordinate the purchase
The provider assesses the buyer. Delivery, acceptance and payout conditions must be met before completion.
terms: An arrangement, not a loan
The underlying customer agreement may be HP or a lease. Explain the actual product rather than presenting vendor finance as a separate type of borrowing.
No assumed acceptance
Offering a finance conversation does not mean every buyer, asset or sale will qualify.
Sales communications
Any finance promotion, quote or use of provider branding needs the appropriate agreement and review.
prepare: Equipment range, suppliers and typical customers
Average sale values, expected volumes and new/used mix
Sales process, delivery terms and desired referral arrangements
faqs: Will Frontier lend to our customers?
No. Frontier arranges funding introductions; the provider decides whether to offer finance and on what terms.
Can we advertise monthly payments?
Only under an agreed process with appropriate, accurate terms and any required disclosures. Do not publish an illustrative quote as a confirmed offer.
Does customer finance fund our stock?
No. A buyer’s finance and your stock facility serve different purposes. A separate stocking arrangement may be needed.
valueHeading: Create a clear route from enquiry to assessment.
valueIntro: We help define how a finance introduction could fit your sales process. Any programme needs agreed product access, responsibilities and customer communications before it is presented as an available arrangement.
